_comment: Well-known credential formats, ported from v1's scanners/secrets/rules.ts. Patterns only: the rules that need judgment (entropy, assignments, connection strings) are Rust, because a regex cannot decide whether a high-entropy string is a secret or a hash. Every rule names the requirements it bears on, so a finding can say which ones it is evidence about rather than leaving the link to be guessed. Rust's regex crate has no lookaround; none of these need it.

rules.title: Anthropic API key found in a file
rules.description: A string starting with sk-ant- (an Anthropic API key) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: Anyone with the file can spend money on your account and read anything sent to the model.
rules.fix: Revoke the key in the Anthropic console, issue a new one, and keep it only in .env.

rules.title: OpenAI API key found in a file
rules.description: A string with the shape of an OpenAI API key (sk-, then T3BlbkFJ in the middle) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it. The shape is gitleaks' openai-api-key rule, without the check of what follows the key, which this scanner does not need.
rules.impact: Anyone with the file can spend money on your account and read anything sent to the model.
rules.fix: Revoke the key on the API keys page of the OpenAI platform, issue a new one, and keep it only in .env.

rules.title: Hugging Face access token found in a file
rules.description: A string with the shape of a Hugging Face access token (hf_ and 34 letters) or organization token (api_org_ and 34 letters) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it. The shapes are gitleaks' huggingface-access-token and huggingface-organization-api-token rules.
rules.impact: Anyone with the file can act as you on Hugging Face: read your private models and datasets, and, with a write token, change them.
rules.fix: Revoke the token in your Hugging Face access token settings, issue a new one, and keep it only in .env.

rules.title: AWS access key ID found in a file
rules.description: A string shaped like an Amazon Web Services access key id (AKIA...) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: Combined with its secret key it gives access to your cloud account.
rules.fix: Deactivate the key in AWS IAM and load credentials from the environment instead.

rules.title: GitHub token found in a file
rules.description: A GitHub personal access token (ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_/github_pat_) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: Grants access to your repositories, possibly with write permission.
rules.fix: Revoke the token on GitHub and, if still needed, create a new one with minimum scopes stored in .env.

rules.title: Slack token found in a file
rules.description: A Slack token (xoxb-/xoxp-/xoxa-/xoxr-/xapp-) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: Lets an attacker read or post messages in your Slack workspace as your app or user.
rules.fix: Revoke the token in Slack and issue a new one stored in .env only.

rules.title: Live Stripe key found in a file
rules.description: A live Stripe key (sk_live_/rk_live_) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: A live secret key can create charges and refunds on your Stripe account.
rules.fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard and keep the new one in .env only.

rules.title: Stripe test key found in a file
rules.description: A Stripe test-mode key (sk_test_/rk_test_) appears in a file. It cannot move money, but it is still a credential kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: Lets anyone read and change the test-mode data on your Stripe account, including test customers and webhooks, and is often a sign the live key is kept the same way.
rules.fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard and keep the new one in .env only, as the live key should be.

rules.title: Google API key found in a file
rules.description: A Google API key (AIza...) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: Can run up charges on your Google Cloud account and use whatever APIs the key is enabled for.
rules.fix: Regenerate the key in Google Cloud Console, restrict it, and store it in .env only.

rules.title: Private key found in a file
rules.description: A private key (a PEM block, an OpenSSH key, or a PGP private key block) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: A private key lets an attacker impersonate your server or decrypt its traffic.
rules.fix: Remove the key from the file, regenerate it, and keep private keys only in certs/ with restrictive permissions.

rules.title: JSON Web Token found in a file
rules.description: A string shaped like a JSON Web Token (eyJ....eyJ....xxxx) appears in a file. A credential in a file is a secret kept in the app's code, where anyone who can read the code, or its history, can use it.
rules.impact: It may be a valid access token for a service; whoever has it can act as its owner until it expires.
rules.fix: Remove the token from the file. Generate tokens at test/run time instead of committing them.

rules.title: SendGrid API key found in a file

rules.impact: Anyone with the file can send email as your app, to anyone, on your account.
rules.fix: Revoke the key in SendGrid's settings, issue a new one, and keep it only in .env.

rules.impact: Anyone with the file can send texts and make calls on your Twilio account, and read its messages.
